clue.text: I agree, within limit, with retraction of earlier work

indicators.note: within tells us the first words sit inside the word for a boundary

blocks.note: taken as written
to nod is to show agreement
a pale is a boundary, as in 'beyond the pale'

explanation.surface: Someone concedes a point, within reason, while withdrawing a book they wrote earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: A pale is an old word for a fence or boundary, as in 'beyond the pale'. A palinode is a poem taking back what an earlier poem said.
explanation.definitionFit: A palinode is a literary recantation, a poem or piece that withdraws statements the author made in a previous composition.

clue.text: Press forward, or back up and shut up

indicators.note: going back means the next word is read from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
the call for silence

explanation.surface: Choose between advancing and retreating quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back up' reads as one phrase meaning support or retreat; the words split into an indicator and the word reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To push is to drive onward or advance determinedly, as in pushing forward with an attack.

clue.text: See attempt at trademark

blocks.note: lo, as in 'lo and behold'
a go is a try

explanation.surface: Look at someone trying to register a brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is a company's emblem or symbol, often registered legally as its brand mark.

clue.text: Successor to 5 and...and bow?

definitions.note: 5 is STRAIT, which sounds like straight

blocks.note: and shortened to 'n', as in rock 'n' roll
the word following bow in bow and arrow

explanation.surface: A riddle about what comes after a cross-reference and after an archer's weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The straight and narrow is the path of virtue, and STRAIT sounds like straight; bow 'n' arrow supplies the same letters a second way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'the straight and narrow' means the path of good conduct, so this word follows 'straight and' in it.

clue.text: D-drops of water meeting old craving for waterway

blocks.note: the stammered first letter of the next word
rain falls as drops of water
aged means old
an itch is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A stuttered account of water drops and an old yearning for a canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A drainage ditch is a channel dug to carry water away from land, a humble kind of watercourse.

clue.text: Artist's work, laced as 3 is minded

definitions.note: the word that stands before 'laced' as NARROW stands before 'minded'

indicators.note: the artist's name is worked over, its letters set out in a fresh order

blocks.note: the word taken as written, its possessive dropped

explanation.surface: A painting, prim and buttoned-up, in the way a narrow-minded person is.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is NARROW: strait-laced matches narrow-minded, both meaning prim and censorious.
explanation.definitionFit: Strait-laced and narrow-minded are parallel compounds, both describing prudish, puritanical people, so the word fills the same slot.

clue.text: I leave the unimportant and I've a shell in three parts

indicators.note: the letter I departs from each of the following words

blocks.note: trivial means unimportant
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A shellfish speaks: it ignores trivia and has a three-part shell.
explanation.walkthrough: One I comes out of each word: TRIVIAL loses its second I, and I'VE loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: A trivalve is a mollusc or shell having three valves, the hinged plates making up a shell.

clue.text: Paint a toad, which is not exactly fitting

indicators.note: not exactly as given means the letters are rendered inaccurately, in a new order

blocks.note: the three words taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Painting a toad is an odd and unsuitable thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Adaptation is the process of adjusting something to suit a purpose or setting, which is a sense of fitting as a noun.

clue.text: Make an alteration in some clothes? Terrific!

indicators.note: only some of the garment word is used, its tail dropped
in places the correction word inside the garment word

blocks.note: an item of clothing
to emend is to correct or alter a text

explanation.surface: A tailor altering garments is cheered on with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some clothes' means only the start of the garment word is used, and the correction sits inside it. 'Alteration' suggests tailoring, but it is correcting a text.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendous used as an exclamation means splendid or great, the same enthusiastic praise as terrific.

clue.text: I produce a sweetener in lumps (Agra version)

indicators.note: a version is a different rendering, so these letters appear in a new form

blocks.note: taken letter for letter
taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A tree speaks, saying it yields sugar in lumps, an Indian city's way of doing it.
explanation.definitionFit: The sugar palm is a tropical tree whose sap is boiled down into jaggery, a sweetener often sold in lumps.

clue.text: Person elected at springtime floor show on river

indicators.note: putting on a show displays the preceding word in a different arrangement

blocks.note: a spring month
taken as written
taken as written
a river in Russia and several in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone voted in during a spring entertainment staged by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor show' reads as cabaret, but show is the anagram signal for floor. The post is directly elected, with polls held in May.
explanation.definitionFit: London's mayor is chosen by popular vote of the capital's citizens, so the office holder is an elected official.

clue.text: Araucaria's time for representation

blocks.note: the setter speaking of himself: Araucaria is = I am, contracted
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: The setter announces it is his moment to stand for something.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's pseudonym in a clue means 'I' or 'me'; here Araucaria's is read as I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a likeness or picture, something that represents a person or object visually.

clue.text: Resilient piece to please the kids

definitions.text: Resilient piece to please the kids

blocks.note: springy, quick to recover shape
a chess piece, also called a rook

explanation.surface: A sturdy toy or chessman meant to delight children.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a springy inflatable structure put up at parties for children to jump on.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflatable play structure shaped like a fortress gives a springy surface on which children jump at fairs and parties.

clue.text: Room for skill with shuttle, perhaps

blocks.note: room as in available area
craft is skill or art

explanation.surface: Space needed for working deftly with a weaver's shuttle.
explanation.walkthrough: A shuttle is a weaving tool, but here the space shuttle.
explanation.definitionFit: The space shuttle was a NASA vehicle for orbital flight, an example of a vessel built to travel beyond Earth.

clue.text: 3 or 25 in 4?

blocks.note: surface: narrow or hidebound, stuck in old views
setter's reading: sitting in a ditch, a trench, so dug in

explanation.walkthrough: 3 is NARROW, 25 HIDEBOUND, 4 DRAINAGE DITCH. Rigid views are firmly fixed; someone in a trench is literally dug in.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrenched means firmly established and hard to shift, describing attitudes that are rigid and narrow.

clue.text: Boat once current across the water

blocks.note: first meaning: a flat-bottomed boat pushed with a pole
second meaning: the former Irish pound, currency across the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A vessel that used to ride the current over the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like flowing water but means currency; from Britain, Ireland is 'across the water', and its pound was replaced by the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a pole-driven river craft and the Irish pound, the monetary unit used in Ireland before the euro.

clue.text: Vexed by burglary?

definitions.note: describes a crime made worse, as in a legal charge

blocks.note: first meaning: annoyed, exasperated
second meaning: the legal term for burglary with a weapon, the more serious charge

explanation.surface: Someone upset at having been burgled.
explanation.walkthrough: Aggravated burglary is the English legal offence of burglary while armed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means irritated in everyday speech, and in law marks an offence made more serious by circumstances such as carrying weapons.

clue.text: Movie lover in ecstasy restrained by class

indicators.note: being restrained means held in, so the first words sit inside the word for class

blocks.note: taken as written
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a hereditary social class

explanation.surface: A film fan in raptures but held back by social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A cineaste is a devotee of films and cinema, someone enthusiastic and knowledgeable about the art of movies.

clue.text: Removed on stretcher, having performed successfully?

blocks.note: first meaning: taken away bodily, as an injured player is
second meaning: from the idiom for pulling off a difficult feat

explanation.surface: A player stretchered off after a triumphant display.
explanation.walkthrough: To carry it off is to succeed at something tricky; the question mark flags that idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means physically taken away, and in the idiom to carry something off means to manage it with success.

clue.text: Vulgar name for endless burden

indicators.note: with no end, the final letter of the word for a load is cut off

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
an onus is a burden or responsibility

explanation.surface: A rude term for a never-ending chore.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is the old British class label for speech or habits not used by the upper class, the U set.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-U described manners or words considered lower-class, so it amounts to common or unrefined in snobbish use.

clue.text: Doctor in storm to take a 15

indicators.note: in places the doctor's letters inside the word for a storm

blocks.note: Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
a strong wind

explanation.surface: A doctor in rough weather goes out in a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking a punt is a British idiom for placing a bet; the surface suggests the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To gamble is to bet or take a chance, which is what having a punt means in British slang.

clue.text: Religious community on holy island left according to custom

blocks.note: a house of nuns
the Scottish island where St Columba founded his monastery
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Nuns living on a sacred island and then departing, as tradition demands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just places CONVENT before the rest. Iona is a small island off western Scotland, long a Christian pilgrimage site.
explanation.definitionFit: Conventional means following accepted practice or tradition, just what acting according to custom describes.

clue.text: Influence rather than 1 down

blocks.note: first meaning: sway or clout
second meaning: the opposite of push, as marked on doors

explanation.definitionFit: Pull means clout or influence, and it is the familiar opposite of push on a door sign.

clue.text: Little boy doing the rounds?

blocks.note: first meaning: a pet form of Edward
second meaning: a swirl of water going round and round

explanation.surface: A small lad making his visits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing the rounds' suggests a paper boy; the question mark points to whirling water.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddy is a diminutive of Edward, and also a whirlpool or current of water that circles back on itself.

clue.text: A sceptic shortly on holy mountain

blocks.note: taken as written
doubting Thomas is the sceptic; Thos is the short form of Thomas

explanation.surface: A doubter, briefly, standing on a sacred peak.
explanation.walkthrough: Thos. is the standard written abbreviation of Thomas, and Doubting Thomas is the apostle who would not believe without proof.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Athos in northern Greece is home to many Orthodox monasteries and is called the Holy Mountain.

clue.text: Very 21 leather next spring

blocks.note: an animal's skin, tanned into leather
a bound is a leap

explanation.surface: A leather item placed beside a coiled spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidebound people cling rigidly to tradition, so the word means extremely conventional and resistant to new ideas.

clue.text: Having been made shipshape, it turned round and departed

indicators.note: turning round means the little word is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: taken as written
the departed are the dead

explanation.surface: A boat was put in order, then swung about and set off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Departed' suggests leaving port; here it is the euphemism for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidied means put in neat order, which is what shipshape means, so the past participle matches.

clue.text: Was the hidden cause of support for carpeting

blocks.note: first meaning: past tense of underlie, to be the basis of something
second meaning: the padding laid beneath a carpet

explanation.surface: Some secret reason lay behind the padding put under a carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: Underlay is the past tense of underlie, to lie beneath as a cause, and also the cushioning sheet laid below carpets.
